title: October 2026 US job openings
question: What will BLS first report for October 2026 total nonfarm job openings, seasonally adjusted, in millions?
resolutionSource: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, Table 1
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first officially published October 2026 observation for BLS series JTS000000000000000JOL: total nonfarm job openings level, seasonally adjusted, corresponding to JOLTS Table 1. Multiply the reported value in thousands by 0.001 and retain precision to 0.001 million. Freeze that first print; subsequent corrections, monthly revisions, and annual revisions do not change the outcome.
drivers: Modest reversion toward the recent first-print mean
Damped decline in openings since May
Weak September payroll growth corroborates soft labor demand
First-print volatility and two-month forecast horizon

reasoning.text: The target is October 2026 total nonfarm job openings on the month's last business day, seasonally adjusted, BLS series JTS000000000000000JOL, Table 1. All openings anchors and historical observations use this same variant. HistoricalContext contains original preliminary prints retrieved from dated BLS archives.

The official calendar at https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/jolts.htm explicitly schedules October 2026 JOLTS for December 1, 2026, at 10:00 AM. It schedules September data for November 3. August is therefore the latest published openings period in this run, leaving two monthly transitions to the target.

reasoning.result: Original first prints, thousands: March 2026 6866; April 7618; May 7594; June 7359; July 7271; August 7079. These yield 6.866, 7.618, 7.594, 7.359, 7.271, and 7.079 million after multiplying by 0.001.

reasoning.text: The base rate is the six consecutive original first prints for March-August 2026. Their mean is 7.297833 million. August's 7.079 million anchors persistence, while the May-August decline of 0.515 million supplies a modest negative momentum update. Original-vintage observations also determine dispersion.

reasoning.call: Open https://www.bls.gov/news.release/jolts.t01.htm and read the seasonally adjusted total and industry rows.
reasoning.result: August 2026 openings were 7079 thousand, versus revised July's 7335 thousand, a decrease of 256 thousand. Professional and business services decreased 119 thousand; health care and social assistance decreased 115 thousand; leisure and hospitality increased 61 thousand.

reasoning.call: Open https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm, the September 2026 Employment Situation released October 2.
reasoning.result: September nonfarm payroll growth was 29000, compared with average monthly growth of 45000 over the preceding 12 months. Unemployment was 4.2 percent. July and August payroll changes were revised down by a combined 60000.

reasoning.text: Level and momentum are modeled separately. September's weak payroll growth corroborates subdued recruiting, supporting the damped negative momentum term. One-off and policy-mechanism adjustments are each zero because the fetched evidence supplies no quantified October effect. The shrinkage coefficients below are judgmental model choices.

Prior/update/interval: Use August persistence plus 25% reversion toward the six-print mean and 25% extrapolation of recent momentum over two months. Level = 7.079; reversion = 0.25*(7.297833-7.079) = +0.054708; momentum = 0.25*2*(7.079-7.594)/3 = -0.085833; one-off = 0; policy = 0. Point = 7.047875, rounded to 7.048 million. The five successive original-print changes are 0.752, -0.024, -0.235, -0.088, and -0.192 million, with mean 0.0426. Sample sigma = 0.405228 million = sqrt(0.6568392/4). The one-month 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 0.518692. Allowing two monthly innovations gives half-width = 1.28*0.405228*sqrt(2) = 0.733541. Bounds = 7.047875 +/- 0.733541 = [6.314334, 7.781416], rounded to [6.314, 7.781]. This approximate Gaussian interval assumes independent monthly innovations; six original prints provide limited calibration.

Upside risk is renewed recruiting or vacancies accumulating faster than firms can fill them. Downside risk is a broader hiring pullback across business services and health care. Outside the interval, an abrupt recruiting surge could produce more than 7.781 million openings, while a sharp contraction in employer demand could push the first print below 6.314 million.
